description.narrative: The development objectives of Promoting Early Childhood Development Project for Uzbekistan are to increase access to early childhood education, improve the quality of learning environments in selected public preschools, and enable a systematic measurement of education quality for informed decision-making. This project has five components. 1) The first component, Improving Quality of Preschool Education, has the following subcomponents: (i) Improving Preschool Education Quality; and (ii) Enhancing System Capacity and Governance. 2) The second component, Increasing Access to Quality Early Learning Environments, aims to support the improvement of quality of early learning environments, as well as non-center based activities for children not enrolled in preschools, which are expected to lead to an increase in access to preschool education. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Improving Early Learning Environments; and (ii) Expanding Access to Early Childhood Education through Alternative Models. 3) The third component, Partnering with the Private Sector through a Social Impact Bond, aims to provide support to the design and implementation of an innovative impact financing approach, a social impact bond (SIB) through partnerships with private providers or preschools. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Supporting the SIB Design and Results Verification; and (ii) Financing the Payment of SIB Results. 4) The fourth component, Establishing an Education Quality Measurement System, aims to support the establishment of a system to measure education quality for informed decision-making in Uzbekistan. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Supporting the Establishment of a Center to Measure and Monitor Quality; and (ii) Developing and Modernizing Student Assessment Systems. 5) The fifth component, Supporting Project Management, aims to support activities related to day-to-day management of the project, its monitoring and auditing.

The project development objectives are to increase access to early childhood education, improve the quality of learning environments in selected public preschools, and enable a systematic measurement of education quality for informed decision-making.

condition.narrative: At all times during the implementation of the Project, the Recipient, through the Ministry of Preschool Education, shall establishand maintain the Project Implementation Unit for the purposes of day-to-day Project management, monitoring and supervision with astaff (including one project coordinator, one financial management specialist, one financial management assistant, one procurementspecialist, and one monitoring and evaluation specialist), resources and terms of reference as thereafter described in the ProjectOperations Manual and all satisfactory to the International Development Association

The Recipient, through the Ministry of Preschool Education, shall carry out the Project in accordance with the requirements,criteria, organizational arrangements and operational procedures set forth in the Legal Agreements and in the Project OperationsManual and Social Impact Bond Operations Manual, and shall not amend, suspend, abrogate or waive any provisions of these ProjectManuals without prior written approval of the International Development Association. In case of any inconsistency between theprovisions of the Project Manuals and those of the Legal Agreements, those of the Legal Agreements shall prevail. Legal Agreementsmean the Financing Agreement for the IDA Credit and the two Co-Financing Grant Agreements for the Project

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning

comment.narrative: EXCEEDED. Aggregated beneficiary data by intervention group (ECE, 1-year mandatory, playgrounds, etc.) for 3 years The indicator includes children from: Preschool preparation groups (713,139) One-year compulsory education groups (357,602) Playground beneficiaries (6-year-old children) – 1,349,017

title.narrative: New children aged 3-7 enrolled in better equipped preschools

comment.narrative: EXCEEDED. A total of 911,631 children enrolled in better-equipped preschools in 2023-2024, along with 4,677 in Learning Hubs and 352,977 in stay groups under the "compulsory preparation" program.

ACHIEVED. Delivery of 22 types of goods was planned for 10,800 preschool classrooms. 20 types have been fully delivered. The remaining 2 types — children's tables and chairs — are expected to reach approximately 9,700 groups by project closing. Given that essential learning and play materials have been fully delivered to all 10,800 classrooms, and the remaining items do not critically affect functionality, the indicator is considered fully achieved.

title.narrative: Families benefitting from home visits supported by the Project

comment.narrative: EXCEEDED. The activity began in October 2021, with a total of 5,121 families involved since then. Of these, 2,071 families have benefited from the home visit program. The yearly breakdown is as follows: 2022: 1,945 families with 730 home visits. 2023: 1,526 families with 643 home visits. 2024: 1,650 families with 736 home visits. 2025: 1,744 families with 1022 visits. Since the beginning of the Project, 2,263 families have benefited from home visits.

title.narrative: Early learning playgroups implemented through the Project

comment.narrative: EXCEEDED. Number of children in playgroups in LHs: 2022 – 48 playgroups 2023 – increased to 62 playgroups 2024 – increased to 80 playgroups (Additionally, playgroups were organized within 3 communities based at schools in Namangan, established outside LH.) 120 playgroups have been established using Aqlvoy buses, with each bus serving four alternative model groups.

title.narrative: Perception of change in gender norms of parents benefiting from the community-based program

comment.narrative: EXCEEDED. The Early Learning Hubs established in Namangan and Samarkand regularly hold meetings with parents on a weekly basis and maintain attendance records. Information collected on discussion topics and feedback from participating parents will enable an assessment of how parental attitudes change in response to program participation and help identify trends related to changing gender norms. A data collection firm has been contracted to design and implement a communications and public relations campaign. Work commenced in February 2025. The final report was submitted and approved in April 2025.

title.narrative: National center for education quality monitoring and measuring

baseline.value: A national center for education quality monitoring and measuring does not exist

target.value: A national center for education quality monitoring and measuring is established and operational

comment.narrative:
ACHIEVED. The National Center for International Research on Education Quality Assessment was established by the Cabinet of Ministers' Resolution No. 997 dated December 8, 2018.
Due to the reorganization in MPSE/APSE, the NCQE was abolished by Presidential Decree No. 128 dated April 20, 2023. All functions related to international assessment have been transferred to the Department of the National Research Institute named after A. Avloniy.
According to Order No. 278 of the Minister of Preschool and School Education, the National Research Institute named after A. Avloniy is now responsible for conducting international research.

actual.value: National center for international researches on education quality assessments was established. Due to reorganization the center was abolished and all functions related to international assessment have been transferred to National research institute named after A. Avloni.

title.narrative: Existing national assessments of student learning outcomes

baseline.value: Existing national assessments of student learning outcomes are not aligned with international good practices, are not standardized, and are not used under a systematic approach

target.value: Completion of an action plan for reviewing and modernizing existing national assessments of student learning outcomes

comment.narrative: ACHIEVED. The modernization of the national assessment system to align with international standards has commenced. With World Bank support, the National Center has conducted two large-scale assessments. Additionally, two consultants were engaged to develop standardized components for assessing learning outcomes and to create a framework for a national assessment system. Due to reorganization, these tasks have now been transferred to the Center for Pedagogical Excellence, Research, and International Assessment at the Ministry. Training sessions for center staff were held in October, and an action plan was developed with support from Oxford AQA.

actual.value: The action plan has been developed.

title.narrative: Public preschools with high-quality learning environments

comment.narrative:
EXCEEDED. A total of 6,213 state preschool institutions across all regions have been equipped with 20 out of the 22 planned types of furniture and educational materials.
The data comes from the 2024 MELE study conducted by the Agency for Preschool Education with World Bank support. The assessment was done in January–March 2024 in 250 public preschools across Uzbekistan. Using the Teach ECE tool, 232 preschools (92.8%) were rated as having "good" or "very good" quality learning environments.

title.narrative: General secondary education quality measurement system

baseline.value: A system to measure general secondary education quality under a systematic approach does not exist

target.value: Systematic measurements of general secondary education quality produced by the new quality assessment system are used to inform plans or policies

comment.narrative: ACHIEVED. PISA 2022 main assessment conducted in April-May 2022 with 202 schools, 7363 students. The results have been published in December 2023. The PIRLS 2021 main assessment was conducted in April 2021 with 180 schools and 5848 students. The results were published on May 19, 2023. Uzbekistan ranked 49 out of 57. TIMSS 2023 field test conducted in March 2022 with 29 schools, 2907 students. The main study was conducted in April-May 2023 with 166 schools and 9000 students. Results were published in December 2024. The TALIS 2024 field trial was conducted in March 2023 with 30 schools, 600 teachers, and 30 directors. The main study was conducted in May 2024. Results will be published in December 2025. According to the ORDER OF THE MINISTER OF PRESCHOOL AND SCHOOL EDUCATION # 278, the National Research Institute for Professional Development of Pedagogues and Training in New Methods named after A. Avloni will be responsible for conducting international research.

actual.value: A system to measure general secondary education quality under a systematic approach established

target.value: Systematic measurements of preschool education quality produced by the new quality assessment system are used to inform plans or policies
